changeSet.sql:
-- Keycloak delivers the email in lowercase at login, so a Benutzer is only found if its email is stored in -- lowercase. Lowercases the emails that are not lowercase yet. Keycloak never delivers these, so their Benutzer -- could not log in with them anyway. Emails already in lowercase stay unchanged. -- Benutzer whose emails differ only in case would end up with the same email. Of these, the Benutzer whose email -- is already lowercase keeps it, otherwise the oldest one gets it. Each of the others gets the first 8 -- characters of its id added before the @, e.g. anna.muster+3f2a9c1e@example.com, which keeps the email unique. -- The part before the @ is shortened, so that it stays within the 64 characters a valid email allows there. UPDATE benutzer SET email = CASE WHEN ranked.rank_in_group = 1 THEN lower(benutzer.email) ELSE left(substring(lower(benutzer.email) FROM '^(.*)@[^@]*$'), 55) || '+' || left(CAST(benutzer.id AS VARCHAR), 8) || substring(lower(benutzer.email) FROM '(@[^@]*)$') END FROM ( SELECT id, row_number() OVER ( PARTITION BY lower(email) ORDER BY (email = lower(email)) DESC, timestamperstellt, id ) AS rank_in_group FROM benutzer ) AS ranked WHERE ranked.id = benutzer.id AND benutzer.email != lower(benutzer.email);
-- Keeps the emails in lowercase from now on. Together with uc_benutzer_email, no two Benutzer can have emails -- that differ only in case. ALTER TABLE benutzer ADD CONSTRAINT chk_benutzer_email_lowercase CHECK (email = lower(email));
